pluss::timeline::rand_between¶

Back to Timeline Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

Timeline pluss::timeline::rand_between(integer_range sizes,
                                       const Timeline& low,
                                       const Timeline& high,
                                       std::uint64_t seed = 0)
Timeline pluss::timeline::rand_between(std::string_view low,
                                       std::string_view high,
                                       integer_range sizes,
                                       std::uint64_t seed = 0)

Sample A Closed Interval Of Instants¶

rand_between() allocates a Timeline with the requested shape and samples each lane uniformly from the closed integer nanosecond interval [low, high]. Both endpoints are eligible. This makes the factory suitable when the upper boundary is itself a valid outcome, and it makes low == high a useful, well-defined constant construction.

The distribution is over representable instants, not displayed calendar labels. Text dates such as "2024-01-01" and "2024-01-03" delimit a continuous interval containing every nanosecond between the two midnights; they do not mean “choose one of three dates.” For whole-day sampling, sample an integer day offset and add pluss::duration::days(offset) to a fixed midnight.

Use random() when the upper endpoint must be excluded. Use full() when a constant result is intentional rather than a degenerate random interval.

Bounds, Shape, And Timezone¶

Timeline bounds must each be rank-zero, defined, and ordered so high >= low. Their stored epoch nanoseconds define the interval. The result carries the lower bound’s timezone metadata, so its fields and default printing use the same civil projection without changing sampled instants.

Text bounds must have the same kind: date with date, time with time, or datetime with datetime. Date-only bounds use midnight; time-only bounds use the Unix epoch date; datetime bounds retain explicit offsets while being stored as absolute epoch nanoseconds.

sizes may describe a scalar or a rank-one, rank-two, or rank-three result. Zero extents are valid and produce an empty Timeline of that shape. Negative extents, rank above three, and element-count overflow are rejected before allocation.

Seeds And Reproducibility¶

A nonzero seed creates a repeatable sequence for the same build and inputs. Seed 0 requests the library’s evolving seed stream; it does not promise the same values on repeated calls. Reproducible examples, tests, and simulations should therefore pass an explicit nonzero seed.

Do not make persisted file formats depend on the exact generated sequence. The contract is uniform closed-interval sampling and same-seed reproducibility, not permanent standardization of a particular random-engine implementation.

Example 1: Equal Bounds Produce A Constant Matrix¶

const auto constant = pluss::timeline::rand_between(
    "2024-02-29", "2024-02-29", {2, 2}, 99);

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(constant, "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["2024-02-29T00:00:00.000000000+00:00", "2024-02-29T00:00:00.000000000+00:00"], 
  ["2024-02-29T00:00:00.000000000+00:00", "2024-02-29T00:00:00.000000000+00:00"]
]

Example 2: Demonstrate The Closed Nanosecond Boundary¶

const auto sampled = pluss::timeline::rand_between(
    {8},
    pluss::timeline::from_epoch(100LL),
    pluss::timeline::from_epoch(102LL),
    99);

std::cout << sampled.epoch_nanos() << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[8], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=8, contiguous=true)
data=[101, 102, 100, 101, 102, 100, 101, 100]

Seeing 102 confirms that the upper endpoint participates. Every lane is one of the three exactly representable ticks; no floating-point conversion is used to select nanoseconds.

Example 3: Verify A Seed Without Depending On Its Particular Values¶

const auto a = pluss::timeline::rand_between(
    "2024-01-01", "2024-01-03", {5}, 7);
const auto b = pluss::timeline::rand_between(
    "2024-01-01", "2024-01-03", {5}, 7);

std::cout << a.epoch_nanos().equal(b.epoch_nanos()) << '\n';

Output¶

true

This is the stable property applications should test. Calling with seed 0 twice is intentionally not the equivalent operation.

Example 4: The Lower Bound Supplies The Display Zone¶

const auto low = pluss::timeline::make("2024-07-01T06:00:00Z")
                     .tz_convert("America/Edmonton");
const auto high = pluss::timeline::make("2024-07-01T06:00:00.000000002Z")
                      .tz_convert("America/Edmonton");
const auto local = pluss::timeline::rand_between({3}, low, high, 5);

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(local, "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["2024-07-01T00:00:00.000000002-06:00", "2024-07-01T00:00:00.000000000-06:00", "2024-07-01T00:00:00.000000000-06:00"]

Failure Modes¶

The call throws for reversed bounds, absent bounds, non-scalar Timeline bounds, mixed text kinds, malformed endpoint text, invalid timezone text, invalid shape, or shape-product overflow. Bounds in different display timezones are still ordered by their absolute epoch nanoseconds; normalize display metadata first if inheriting the lower bound’s zone would surprise the reader.

Sampling allocates contiguous storage and performs one random draw per output lane, so time and storage are both linear in numel().

See Also¶

  • random: sample the half-open interval [low, high).

  • full: allocate a known constant instant.

  • from_epoch: construct exact integer nanosecond bounds.
